status_note: Candidate associations. Statuses: 'pending' = not yet checked; 'reference_checked' = a named scholarly reference was read and supports the stated point, but the primary text is NOT yet checked; 'verified' = primary locator and edition checked (only then may the record enter public.ancient_sources). The Sources panel displays only 'verified' rows, so none of these appear on the site.

records.candidate_source: Jacob of Serugh, homily on the Seven Sleepers (Syriac, c. 450-521); earlier lost Greek source
records.dating_note: Jacob of Serugh (d. 521) homily, derived from a lost Greek source (per secondary literature; homily not yet read in primary text)
records.shared: Youths hide in a cave to escape persecution and sleep for a long period
records.differs: Qur'an leaves the number of sleepers open (3, 5 or 7); Syriac versions name specific numbers that vary by tradition
records.required_check: Read the Syriac or English text of the Jacob of Serugh homily (Bedjan edition, cited by Witztum n.11) and cite the section on the sleepers
records.checked_against: Encyclopaedia Iranica, "Ephesus, Seven Sleepers of" (Sims-Williams 1998): Quranic number left open (3, 5 or 7; 4, 6 or 8 counting the dog). Witztum (The Syriac milieu of the Quran, PDF on almuslih.org) notes Jacob of Serugh died 521.

records.story: Seven Sleepers: dog at the cave entrance
records.candidate_source: Theodosius, Pilgrimage (518-530) as cited in secondary literature
records.shared: Unverified hypothesis: a dog motif may occur in the cited pilgrimage tradition; primary passage not yet inspected.
records.differs: No reliable comparison can be stated until the primary pilgrimage passage and its wording are checked.
records.required_check: Confirm the dog detail in the primary Pilgrimage text before citing

records.story: Dhu al-Qarnayn and the Syriac Alexander Legend
records.dating_note: Alexander Homily c. 630-640 (Gero and van Bladel, as cited by Witztum). Wikipedia gives 629-636 for the Syriac Legend; the two dates should not be merged
records.shared: A ruler travels to the ends of the world, builds a barrier against Gog and Magog
records.differs: The Qur'an does not name Alexander; the Legend names him
records.required_check: Read the Syriac Legend text (Budge edition or van Bladel study) and cite the barrier passage
records.checked_against: Witztum (Syriac milieu of the Quran), p.14 n.33: van Bladel's study of the Alexander legend in Q 18:83-102 is cited; p.14-15 n.35: Alexander Homily dated c. 630-640 by Gero and van Bladel

records.dating_note: Genesis Rabbah is generally assigned to Late Antiquity (commonly fifth-century redaction, with dating debated); the date of the extant manuscript witnesses must be distinguished from the date of composition. The prior claim that the surviving text postdates the Qur'an was unsupported.
records.shared: Abraham destroys idols in his father's shop; the largest idol survives
records.differs: Qur'an 21:58 describes leaving the largest idol; Genesis Rabbah 38:13 places the idols in Terah's shop. Qur'an 6:74 names Azar; the midrash uses Terah. Qur'an 21:51-70 does not name Nimrod.
records.required_check: Compare the complete Hebrew/English Genesis Rabbah 38:13 (Sefaria; critical Theodor-Albeck edition if accessible) with Qur'an 21:51-70, and document edition, translation, and textual witness before promotion.
records.checked_against: Hebrew text of Genesis Rabbah 38:13 (Rabbi Hiyya, grandson of Rabbi Ada of Yafo) quoted in a published Sicha Conversation PDF; English summaries in Steinsaltz Center and Wikipedia name Terah, the stick, and the largest idol. Full critical edition (Theodor-Albeck) not yet read.

records.dating_note: Genesis Rabbah redacted c. 5th-6th century; Cave of Treasures Syriac, date disputed
records.shared: Angels bow to Adam after his creation
records.differs: The scene is absent from the canonical Genesis text
records.required_check: Confirm the bowing episode in the cited passages of each text

records.candidate_source: Persecution at Najran under Dhu Nuwas, c. 523-524 (Simeon of Beth Arsham letter, 524)
records.dating_note: Event dated 520s CE; identification with Qur'an 85 contested (Daniel 3 reading argued by Silverstein, Der Islam 2019)
records.shared: Believers burned in a trench by a ruler for refusing to renounce their faith
records.differs: Qur'an does not name Najran or Dhu Nuwas; the identification is a later scholarly and exegetical proposal
records.required_check: Read Walters 2021 pp. 88-103 (or Shahid 1971) and cite the passage on the persecution; confirm the author attribution in Silverstein's article (Der Islam 96(2)) before citing him by name
records.checked_against: Der Islam 96(2):281-323 (2019), "Who are the Aṣḥāb al-Ukhdūd? Q 85:4-10 in Near Eastern Context": argues the historical reading points to Daniel 3, not Najran. Author attribution to Silverstein is from the record ID and was not confirmed on the page Simeon's letter: Syriac letter written from Hirta, January 524; English translation in J. Edward Walters, 'Simeon of Beth Arsham, Letter on the Himyarite Martyrs', Eastern Christianity: A Reader (Eerdmans, 2021), pp. 88-103 (per Wikipedia citation; not yet read).

records.dating_note: Britannica: no evidence of a true hanif cult; reports are mostly later
records.shared: Figures who rejected idols before Islam
records.differs: Qur'an uses hanif of Abraham; the reports name later individuals
records.required_check: Cite Rubin 1990 (JSAI 13) for the historical discussion; read the passage before quoting
records.checked_against: Britannica "hanif": "There is no evidence that a true hanif cult existed in pre-Islāmic Arabia", and certain individuals repudiated the old gods without joining Judaism or Christianity

records.story: Claim that a foreigner taught Muhammad
records.candidate_source: Qur'an's own report of the accusation; later exegesis names Yasar and Jabr
records.dating_note: The accusation is in the Qur'an; the names come from later tafsir
records.shared: A claim that the Qur'an came from a human teacher with access to scripture
records.differs: The Qur'an rejects the claim; the names are not in the verse
records.required_check: Verify the names Yasar and Jabr against Wahidi or Ibn Kathir; present as later tradition, not the verse
